name: connors_rsi_extreme_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: Connors RSI combines three oscillators (RSI, streak RSI, percentile rank) into a composite that identifies extreme short-term oversold conditions. When CRSI < 10 on liquid stocks near VWAP, the bounce probability is elevated because the sell-off is typically driven by short-term momentum traders who will quickly reverse. Inefficiency persists because CRSI is less commonly used than standard RSI, and the signal is infrequent enough that most automated systems don't bother.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.
weaknesses: CRSI on 1-min bars is extremely noisy. The 3-bar RSI oscillates wildly — signals fire frequently and many are false.
Thin profit factor (1.13) means a small increase in costs or slippage turns the strategy negative.
In trending markets, CRSI can stay at extremes for 50+ bars — the 'extreme' signal is not extreme at all, it's the trend.
prior_art: Connors RSI — Larry Connors / TradingMarkets. Well-published. Adapted to intraday 1-min from original daily/swing timeframe.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
